ads_analysis.account_level_diagnosis: The account is primarily budget-constrained across the revenue-driving non-brand and shopping portfolio: 5 in-scope campaigns are sitting at ~99.9% budget utilization while losing ~78–83% impression share to budget with 0% lost to rank at the campaign level (e.g., Shopping - Apparel: 18% IS, 82% lost to budget, 0% lost to rank; Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo: 21% IS, 79% lost to budget, 0% lost to rank). Brand is the one exception: it has headroom (75.4% budget utilization) but still loses 40% to budget, suggesting daily pacing/caps rather than true monthly constraint. Incremental growth should come from reallocating/raising budgets in the strongest shopping lines and stopping waste/leakage (competitor zero-click queries and negative conflicts) before simply scaling everything.
notable_patterns: Most scalable campaigns are capped: Shopping - Apparel/Electronics/Home & Garden/Beauty all run at 99.9% budget utilization with 80–83% impression share lost to budget and 0% lost to rank, while IS sits only 17–20%.

Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo is also hard-capped (99.9% budget utilization; 79% lost to budget; 21% IS) despite strong avg quality score (8.8), implying demand is there but budget is the throttle.

Brand efficiency is excellent (Brand Search - GR ROAS 24.26 on €494.34 spend, 121.2 conversions) and not rank-limited (0% lost to rank), yet it still shows 40% lost to budget while only using 75.4% of its budget—consistent with intra-day caps/pacing rather than poor eligibility.

Query mix is polluted by competitor-brand lookups that don’t generate clicks: 2,058 zero-click competitor-brand impressions and 56.1% of search-term impressions coming from zero-click competitor terms (e.g., “delphi retail group”, “marathon mercantile”), creating measurable wasted reach without conversion upside.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Scale is being throttled by budget, not rank: 19% impression share with 81% lost to budget and 0% lost to rank while running at 99.9% budget utilization; ROAS is the best among Shopping at 4.34 on €382.90 spend.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase budget first here (or reallocate from weaker areas) to capture the 81% budget-lost share while maintaining ROAS guardrails.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Also budget-capped (99.9% utilization; 80% lost to budget; 20% IS) with strong efficiency (ROAS 4.53), but weaker avg quality score (5.7) suggests feed/title optimization could reduce CPC as you scale.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Add budget, but pair with product data/feed improvements to lift quality and protect ROAS as volume increases.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Demand is being cut off by budget (21% IS; 79% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization) despite a very strong avg quality score (8.8); additionally, this is where negative conflicts are blocking an estimated 6,940 impressions.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Fix negative-keyword conflicts first, then raise/reallocate budget to regain the 79% budget-lost share with high-QS traffic.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Heavily budget-limited (19% IS; 81% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization) with ROAS 4.91; this is a scalable line but should be expanded after plugging query leakage and ensuring product coverage is prioritized.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Increase budget selectively (or reallocate) after tightening query controls and ensuring the highest-margin categories are emphasized.

campaign_findings.diagnosis: Extremely budget-throttled (18% IS; 82% lost to budget; 99.9% utilization) but lowest ROAS among the material shopping set (3.33), so scaling should follow efficiency fixes rather than a pure budget raise.
campaign_findings.recommended_action: Improve efficiency (product segmentation, bids/targets, exclude weak queries/products) before giving it the same budget priority as higher-ROAS shopping lines.

recommendation_cards.title: Reallocate/raise budgets on the strongest capped campaigns (Home & Garden, Beauty, Performance Max) before scaling everything
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Multiple campaigns are hard-capped at ~99.9% budget utilization while losing ~80%+ impression share to budget and 0% to rank: Shopping - Home & Garden (81% lost to budget, ROAS 4.34), Shopping - Beauty (80%, ROAS 4.53), Performance Max - Full Catalog (81%, ROAS 4.91). This is the clearest incremental volume lever in the account.
recommended_steps: Increase daily budgets (or reallocate from lower-priority areas) first to Shopping - Home & Garden and Shopping - Beauty, then Performance Max - Full Catalog.
Set ROAS guardrails at the campaign level (use the last-quarter baselines: 4.34–4.91) and ramp budgets in steps rather than all at once.
Keep Shopping - Apparel budget increases conditional on efficiency improvements (it’s capped too, but at ROAS 3.33).
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Budget-lost impression share falling from ~80–83% toward <50% in the scaled campaigns while maintaining ROAS at/above current levels (≥4.3 in Home & Garden/Beauty; ≥4.9 in Performance Max).

recommendation_cards.title: Resolve negative-keyword conflicts that are blocking your own demand in Non-Brand Search
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: There are 3 negative conflicts blocking an estimated 6,940 impressions, all in “Non-Brand Search - Seasonal Promo”: negative 'free' blocks “free shipping promo code” (5,200 blocked impressions), 'DIY' blocks “kitchen appliances clearance DIY install” (980), and 'returns' blocks “winter jacket sale returns policy” (760). This is on top of the campaign already losing 79% impression share to budget.
recommended_steps: In the negative-keyword conflicts report, replace broad/phrase negatives ('free', 'DIY', 'returns') with tighter match types or move them to a more appropriate scope so they don’t block intended promo/seasonal traffic.

Create a dedicated ‘policy/support intent’ exclusion list only where needed (e.g., keep 'returns' excluded for sales ad groups if it truly underperforms, but don’t block mixed-intent terms like “winter jacket sale returns policy” without testing).
After conflicts are cleared, reassess query performance and only then increase budgets to capture incremental eligible impressions.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Eligible impressions in Non-Brand Search rising by ~6.9k+ per period (directionally) and conversion volume increasing from the current 18.5 without a disproportionate ROAS drop (currently 3.88).

recommendation_cards.title: Add competitor-brand negatives to stop zero-click impression waste (and protect budgets for converting queries)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Competitor-brand leakage is substantial and unproductive: 2,058 competitor-brand zero-click impressions, with 56.1% of search-term impressions coming from zero-click competitor terms (e.g., “delphi retail group”, “marathon mercantile”, “ionian goods co”, “acropolis retail quote”), and no competitor-brand terms listed as converting.
recommended_steps: Add competitor names as negatives (starting with the listed terms) in non-brand search and any catalog/automated campaigns where query matching is broad.
Keep brand-conquesting off unless you can demonstrate conversion value; otherwise route budget to capped, proven campaigns.
Re-check the search-term report after 7 days to confirm competitor queries’ impression share drops materially.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Share of impressions from the identified competitor-brand terms dropping from 56.1% to <20% (or as low as feasible) and a corresponding improvement in click-through and conversion rate.

recommendation_cards.title: Fix rank loss on high-quality keywords that are still losing auctions (selective bid/target adjustments)
recommendation_cards.what_data_shows: Some high-quality keywords are still losing impression share to rank: “holiday electronics deals” (QS 7.5, IS 19%, lost rank 81%), “winter jacket sale” (QS 8.0, IS 21%, lost rank 79%), and “pilot account promo code” (QS 9.5, IS 58%, lost rank 42%). This indicates isolated bid/Ad Rank issues even though campaign-level lost rank is reported as 0% in the summary.
recommended_steps: Segment these terms into tighter ad groups and raise bids/loosen targets only for these high-QS, high-intent keywords (not across the whole campaign).
Align ad copy and landing-page messaging to these exact intents to preserve QS while lifting Ad Rank.
Use auction positioning diagnostics to ensure the incremental bid actually increases top-of-page presence for these terms.
recommendation_cards.what_to_watch: Impression share on these keywords moving from ~19–21% toward 30%+ and lost-to-rank falling from ~79–81% toward <50% without CPA/CVR deterioration.

already_working: Ad creation isn’t a bottleneck: 100% of ads are rated Good or Excellent (4 Excellent, 4 Good).

Auction presence vs named competitors is competitive overall: avg outranking share is 52.9% and self top-of-page rate (49.6%) exceeds competitors’ (42.4%) on average—this points away from a broad rank crisis.

Brand Search - GR is highly efficient (ROAS 24.26; 121.2 conversions on €494.34 spend) with 0% impression share lost to rank, so core brand performance is healthy; the main issue is capturing more eligible demand via budget/pacing.

market_mapping.why_now_summary: Retail search demand and spend in Greece are growing QoQ while the account is only capturing ~17–21% impression share in key revenue-driving Shopping and non-brand campaigns due almost entirely to budget (≈80%+ lost to budget, 0% lost to rank). At the same time, competitors are visibly active and allocating meaningful spend share across Search/Shopping, so staying budget-capped now likely concedes incremental demand and share-of-voice during an expanding market. This creates immediate urgency to (1) reallocate/raise budgets in the highest-ROAS capped Shopping/PMax lines and (2) stop known query leakage (competitor zero-click + negative conflicts) so added budget converts rather than being wasted.

supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: Another large spender (19%) active in Search implies sustained competition; when your best-performing campaigns are capped, the opportunity cost of not buying available impressions is higher right now.

supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: At 11.0% spend share vs much larger competitors (e.g., 24% and 19%), the account is structurally under-invested in the auction; this supports urgency to remove internal throttles (budget caps/pacing) in the highest-ROAS campaigns to defend and grow share.

supporting_facts.fact: Keyword “winter jacket sale” index: Q4 2025 = 100, Q2 2026 = 98, Q3 2026 = 121 (Growth = 21%).
supporting_facts.relevance_to_recommendation: One of the account’s identified high-intent terms is growing (+21%), reinforcing that near-term seasonal/non-brand demand is rising; resolving negative conflicts and easing budget caps now helps avoid missing the upswing for these queries.

email_copy.subject: EUR 12,644 sitting behind budget caps (21.29% IS; 78.7% lost to budget)
email_copy.hook:
From what I’m seeing in your paid search account, performance isn’t being held back by ad quality or auction rank — it’s being throttled by budget pacing in the exact campaigns that already drive revenue.

Right now you’re effectively choosing not to show up for a large share of ready-to-buy searches in Greece, even when you’re eligible to win them.
why_now_bullets: Greek retail search is expanding right now: spend is up 9.0% QoQ and query demand is up 6.0% QoQ — but your key campaigns are only capturing 21.29% impression share.
The account is losing 78.7% impression share to budget with 0.0% lost to rank — meaning the constraint is internal (caps/pacing), not competitiveness.
Competitors are visibly funding the auction: one holds 24% spend share and another 19%, while this account sits at 11.0% — staying capped now compounds the gap.
email_copy.stat_sub: Backed by budget-lost impression share in your strongest non-brand + shopping lines
email_copy.impact_line: There’s an estimated EUR 12,644 available this quarter simply from removing the current bottleneck: your account is running on a EUR 420 daily budget while the portfolio is constrained almost entirely by budget (not rank). The fastest path to that lift is to fund the highest-ROAS capped campaigns first, and tighten the few leaks that would otherwise soak up any added spend.

email_copy.cards_intro: Here are the specific moves that unlock volume without “just spending more” — first fix the blockers (conflicts/leakage), then scale the campaigns that are already proving efficient.
email_copy.working_intro: Also worth calling out what’s solid: the account fundamentals are healthy, so this is a scaling/pacing problem — not a rebuild.
email_copy.opportunity_intro: If we lift coverage from today’s 21.29% toward the market’s 35.0% benchmark, the incremental traffic estimates below show the top-of-funnel needed to support the EUR 12,644 upside — with click rate modeled conservatively.
email_copy.fix_title: Want me to map the exact budget + cleanup sequence for you?
email_copy.fix_body: Reply with “A” and I’ll send a tight 7-day action plan you can implement immediately, or reply with “B” and I’ll send a paced 3-week ramp plan (with guardrails). If you prefer, just reply “A” or “B”.
email_copy.ps: P.S. One quick win: you have campaigns losing budget share while losing 0.0% to rank — that’s the rare case where scaling is mostly a controls problem, not an efficiency mystery.
